victims.summary: Everest ransomware group claims Stadler Rail’s database was leaked, exposing about 201 GB of data and roughly 271,868 files. The leaked material is described as including passenger-information system materials, train-system components, and related onboard runtime components and train-system configuration files. The leak post identifies stadlerrail.com as the victim domain and lists Java, Python and PowerShell as platforms. ThreatCluster’s news reporting notes Stadler Rail reportedly rejected a ransom demand of CHF 10 million (about $12.3 million) after a breach of a supplier data-exchange platform, with the incident described as occurring in mid-July 2026.

victims.summary: Everest group claims Keysight Technologies' data archive includes source code, Git repositories, test platforms, automation systems, firmware, release packages, configurations, diagnostic archives, and engineering materials, totaling about 489 GB on disk (roughly 1.38 TB unpacked and about 1.05 million files). The leak post states the publication status is published and that the files will be released after a countdown; the ransom note notes the company still has time to contact the group. Victim is Keysight Technologies; the material is described as encompassing LTE, 5G NR, O-RAN, UE emulation, test-lab management, network-load generation, radio interfaces and related engineering tooling.
